title: Agencies and the fifty percent cut
summary: Booking agencies demanded fifty percent of the band; he refused at first with the William Morris Agency but then went with Moe Gale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, Cootie, let's first -- first let me ask you, were you with Mo Gale, or were you with Shaw?
No. I was with the William Morris Agency in the beginning.
And was Willard with the agency then?
So I wasn't getting no work. Then I
had tried to scuffle this thing with my band alone.
Tried to do your own booking, you mean?
No. Tried to do my own handling my band, you know.
So, during that period of time, you had to give up some part of your band in order to be a success.
So I said, 'Well, I ain't going to give up no part of my band.' And it squares me out. So that's the time I came in with Moe Gale.
Oh. Well, Cootie who were you dealing with there?
Yeah. You know, when they were talking to you and telling you how you had to be commercial and this, that and the other.
No. I didn't have to be commercial.
Well, what were they telling you, then?
About that you had to give up part of your band. Fifty percent.
So -- who was doing it -- I think Cab. He had to give up fifty percent of his.
Who else? All the bands around -- Jimmy Lunsford. No, he didn't give up nothing, so they squared him out. Burned the place down where he was at.
And everybody around. Harry James. He was stewed, then. He couldn't make it. Everybody owned him. And so I went and gave up fifty percent of my band.
